title: U.S. Senate · Virginia

context.text: The Democratic primary was canceled and incumbent Mark Warner advanced unopposed. Bert Mizusawa won the Republican primary on August 4, 2026 with 51.5% of the vote, defeating David Williams (28.9%) and Kim Farington (19.6%).
Independent candidate Mark Moran withdrew from the general election and is not on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot.

priorities.text: Says he has worked to strengthen America's economy and "spearheaded the largest infrastructure investments in half a century" and expanded Virginia's domestic manufacturing.
Cites work to lower health care costs for Virginia families.

Cites his work on the Senate Intelligence Committee, where he served as chairman in 2021-2022 and serves as vice chairman in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), as central to "protecting the highest levels of America's national security."

positions.summary: Cosponsored S. 1531, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, a bill "to regulate assault weapons, to ensure that the right to keep and bear arms is not unlimited."

Cosponsored S. 2150, the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025, a bill to protect a person's ability to determine whether to continue or end a pregnancy and a provider's ability to provide abortion services.
Cosponsored S. 46, the Health Care Affordability Act of 2025, a bill to expand eligibility for the refundable credit for coverage under a qualified health plan.
Cosponsored S. 5390, the End Trump's Tariff Tax Act, a bill to terminate and refund certain duties imposed by the President.
In a February 2026 statement on U.S. military action in Iran, said the decision to take the nation to war rests with Congress and criticized the president for not seeking congressional authorization.
positions.quote: The Constitution is clear: the decision to take this nation to war rests with Congress

record.text: Serves on the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs (Ranking Member, Subcommittee on Securities, Insurance, and Investment); the Committee on Finance; the Committee on Rules and Administration; the Select Committee on Intelligence (Vice Chairman); and the Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Bert Mizusawa
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 51.5% of the vote

priorities.text: Says he will be an "authoritative voice on national security policy and efficient defense spending" as a combat veteran in the Senate.
priorities.quote: Will be av respected, authoritative voice on national security policy and efficient defense spending. Combat veteran in US Senate.

priorities.text: Says the country is "a nation of laws" that must "enforce the law uniformly."
priorities.quote: We are a nation of laws and must enforce the law uniformly

positions.summary: Campaign website (quoted on Ballotpedia) says he will defend the right to keep and bear arms and fight any effort to infringe on it.
positions.quote: I will defend our rights to citizen self-defense and fight any effort to infringe on that right.

statements.quote: We must keep our borders secure while making legal immigration for those seeking the American Dream available. Those who broke the law and came here illegally should not be given a free path to citizenship over those choosing to do it legally.
statements.context: In a June 2026 Charlottesville Tomorrow questionnaire for Republican U.S. Senate primary candidates

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign site (bertforsenate.com) platform page lists fiscal responsibility, affordability, veterans, stock-trading ban, health care costs and nuclear energy, none of which takes a side on the guide's issue statements. He gave no answers to the VPM/public-radio candidate Q&A. The Charlottesville Tomorrow primary questionnaire supplied one statement (immigration). His data-center answer about the Green New Deal is not shown because it is about data centers rather than a fossil-fuel transition.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has documented positions on the fixed issue keys via a direct statement, vote, or questionnaire answer found in this research; positions are left empty rather than inferred from party. Bert Mizusawa's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey text contains minor typos in the original source, reproduced verbatim in quotes. Biography gaps: Mark Warner's Senate biography pages were fetched; Bioguide could not be loaded (blocked), so Ballotpedia and his Senate office were used. Bert Mizusawa's own campaign site could not be loaded, so his biography relies on Ballotpedia, including his Candidate Connection survey; the 41-year service figure is his own description, while Ballotpedia dates his Army service 1979-2016.
